title: Romanov's theorem: the integers of the form p + 2^k have positive lower density, with Erdős' complement, after Romanov 1934 and Erdős 1950
summary: A Lean 4 proof, with no unproved steps, of the theorem of N. P. Romanov, Über einige Sätze der additiven Zahlentheorie, Math. Ann. 109, 1934: the integers p + 2^k, p prime, have positive lower density, for k >= 0 and for k >= 1. With it, the result of P. Erdős, On integers of the form 2^k + p and some related problems, Summa Brasil. Math. 2, 1950: by a covering system, every 119477317 + 346729110 t is odd and is not p + 2^k, so the odd numbers that are not of that form also have positive lower density.
